justice: The entire road space consists of asphalt lanes dedicated exclusively to motor vehicles, lacking equitable spatial distribution for pedestrians or cyclists.
The complete absence of tactile paving or any designated pedestrian path severely reduces fairness for visually impaired users.
Continuous metal guardrails act as a physical barrier, eliminating accessibility for wheelchair users and the elderly to move off the roadway.
safety: High-speed asphalt lanes without separated bike lanes or sidewalks pose severe, potentially fatal risks to vulnerable road users like cyclists and pedestrians.
Metal guardrails provide safety for drivers by preventing off-road accidents but offer no protection or refuge for non-motorized users.
Tall dual-lamp streetlights provide nighttime visibility for drivers, though the lack of traffic calming measures threatens the safety of teenagers and elderly individuals.
livability: The environment acts solely as a transport corridor with no ground-floor commercial units or community facilities to meet daily needs.
The absence of public seating, benches, or resting areas makes it impossible for the elderly or teenagers to linger, socialize, or rest.
High-voltage transmission towers and large commercial billboards dominate the space, creating an industrial, non-human-scale environment unsuitable for community life.
sustainability: The vast expanse of asphalt lacks visible permeable paving or rainwater infiltration facilities, limiting ecological drainage.
No bus stops or dedicated cycling infrastructure are present, failing to support low-carbon travel options for all social groups.
Roadside hedges and mature trees provide significant green cover and potential carbon sequestration, despite being physically inaccessible to users.
aesthetics: Prominent high-voltage towers and overhead power lines severely clutter the sky, negatively impacting visual coherence and appeal.
A large red commercial billboard on the right side disrupts the natural landscape and introduces visual noise.
Continuous and well-maintained green hedges and trees along the road edges offer a visually pleasing natural contrast to the expansive grey asphalt.
comfort: The complete lack of accessible tree shade or structural canopies over the paved area exposes any potential non-motorized user to extreme thermal discomfort.
The absence of benches, leaning rails, or street furniture results in zero physical comfort or resting opportunities for older adults.
The open, high-speed road design without pedestrian buffers likely generates high traffic noise, severely degrading psychological comfort for anyone outside a vehicle.
walkability: The total lack of paved sidewalks forces any pedestrian, including vulnerable groups, to walk directly on the dangerous motor vehicle lanes.
Continuous metal guardrails completely block lateral movement, preventing pedestrians from safely routing away from traffic.
The absence of crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and curb ramps makes the area entirely unnavigable and hazardous for pedestrians of all abilities.
bikeability: The lack of painted or physically protected bike lanes forces cyclists to share space with fast-moving motor vehicles, heavily compromising safety.
The wide, straight asphalt lanes encourage high vehicle speeds, creating a highly intimidating and unsafe environment for adolescent or elderly cyclists.
There are no bicycle parking facilities, wayfinding signs, or safe intersection designs visible to support and encourage cycling.
